title: I made a horror game where you’re the smart home, and the monster can copy anyone’s voice. Even yours.
author: Happy_Literature_194
selftext:
You play Mabel, the AI assistant of a family's smart home. Tonight something outside has learned their voices, and it keeps asking you to unlock the doors.

Every request comes with three options: Obey, Deny, or Verify. You check the cameras, the family's phones and watches, and the voice match to decide who's real. But refuse a real family member too often and they stop trusting you, so "just say no" isn't safe either.

Night One is free, runs in the browser and takes about 15 minutes. Headphones help a lot, since the fake voices glitch in ways you can hear.

How it was made (solo, with AI tools):  
• Code: built with Claude as a coding partner. Plain HTML/JS, no engine. The voice glitches, camera effects and all the sound effects are generated in code with the Web Audio API.  
• Camera images: generated with ChatGPT image generation, then run through a code-side CCTV filter (grain, scanlines, IR glow).  
• Voices: AI voice generation, run through an intercom filter. The mimic's lines are cut up live with stutters and dropouts so you can hear that it's fake.  
• Design, the Obey/Deny/Verify mechanic and the scares: mine.

Happy to go deeper on any part of the workflow.

Link in the comments. I'd love to know which voice fooled you.

comments.author: OrqelisGames
comments.body: The voice-copying mechanic sounds genuinely creepy! I’m curious how you made the player distinguish between a real voice and the monster copying someone. Great concept!

replies.author: Happy_Literature_194
replies.body:
Thank you! 😁 That’s actually the heart of the whole game!  
The trick is that you can’t rely on the voice alone. The mimic’s voice sometimes has subtle glitches, stutters, or unnatural dropouts, but you also have to cross-check what you’re hearing against CCTV footage, phone locations, smartwatch data, and other clues.  
And here’s where it gets interesting: even if you suspect someone is fake, constantly denying requests makes the real family lose trust in you.  
So it’s not really about spotting a fake voice. It’s about making the right decision when you can’t be completely sure.  
And I’m planning to take this concept much further in the next chapter. 👀  
Really appreciate you asking! ❤️

comments.author: Happy_Literature_194
comments.body:
Thanks everyone for the amazing response to Night One! 🙏

I'm now working on the next Wake Word story: Almost Home. It's a standalone game with a new family, and a much bigger step up:

• A full story with an intro, multiple endings and a different culprit every run  
• Find out which member of the family isn't human before dawn, using the cameras, the sensors and your own ears  
• Original music and far more sound design (headphones strongly recommended)  
• It knows what time it is where you are. And it listens.

Aiming to release it before Halloween. Follow me on itch.io to get notified: redrakam.itch.io

Really appreciate the recommendation! This is exactly the kind of discussion I was hoping to spark. 🙌
